#2013. SCOTLAND 2 NORTH MACEDONIA 1: John McGinn at the double to spare the blushes of Pocognoli's shaky Scots on skipper Robertson's big night

By JOHN MCGARRY, SCOTTISH CHIEF SPORTS FEATURE WRITER

Published: 17:01 EST, 13 November 2026 | Updated: 17:11 EST, 13 November 2026

On the night when the nation looked over its shoulder and celebrated the past, the here and now for Scotland looked distinctly uncertain.

Coming 40 years and a day after his friend, Sir Kenny Dalglish, pulled on a Scotland jersey for the 102nd and final time, Andy Robertson joined the great man on a mark which, for years, seemed beyond the reach of mere mortals.

By time up, history had mercifully repeated itself at Hampden. Back in the day, Dalglish, by then player-manager at Anfield, sailed into the international sunset on the back of a routine 3-0 win over Luxembourg.

Facing another opponent of modest ability, Robertson’s red letter day didn’t go quite as smoothly. Yet, when the Tottenham man is old and grey and reflecting on the night he created history, the annals will at least record a slender victory.

While his side did just about enough to prevail here, this was another fraught night for Sebastien Pocognoli.

You can talk about the need for patience under the new manager until the cows come home. But North Macedonia are 71st in FIFA’s rankings. Scotland are 43rd.

John McGinn celebrates in trademark fashion after netting Scotland's winner from the spot

At Hampden Park, in front of an expectant crowd, Scotland should be putting them to the sword with something to spare.

Yet, for long enough, the Belgian’s new-look side were flat, predictable and plodding. It said much that it took the intervention of VAR for them to get the penalty which would ultimately lead to three points being accrued.

John McGinn’s second half double saved the Belgian’s blushes and truthfully there was little else to get the Tartan Army off their seats.

Too many big-name players scarcely merited pass marks. Too few looked comfortable in the system the manager is trying to bed in.

If it was a step in the right direction, it was a small one. After five games under the affable Belgian, the progress has certainly not been startling.

While it goes without saying that beating the Swiss in St Gallen on Monday will be an inordinately tougher task, having some hope of moving up a place and securing a kinder draw for the Euros is still better than no hope.

Regardless of what pot they end up in when the draw is made in Belfast next month, a radical improvement will certainly be required across the board if they are to stand any chance of qualifying for the tournament via the front door.

As well as the achievements of Robertson and Dalglish, the career of Craig Gordon was acknowledged before the match with the 84-times capped keeper deservedly afforded a warm hand by the Tartan Army.

McGinn slots home his penalty after Ben Gannon-Doak had been brought down in the area

There were absolutely no excuses for Scotland here. North Macedonia were a tier-two team in name only. They arrived at Hampden having not won in 12 matches and not scored in eight.

Another Pocognoli game saw another back-three combination. This time Luke Graham was selected in the centre of the unit with Ryan Porteous and Kieran Tierney deployed either side of the Stoke man in what were their first appearances under the Belgian.

Robertson and Ben Gannon-Doak were tasked with providing the width in the 3-4-3. Scott McTominay slotted back into an advanced role beside John McGinn with the returning Che Adams asked to lead the line.

For all there was a healthy crowd in excess of 40,000 inside Hampden, the atmosphere was subdued. In the four Nations League games to date under the new manager, the side hadn’t exactly given the supporters much to feed off.

Despite some big guns returning, Scotland made a laboured start to their night’s work. It said much that Graham, on his second appearance, was busier than any defender in white.

The first opening came as a result of an opposition error. John McGinn found Billy Gilmour who fed the overlapping Robertson. The skipper’s cross was well out of Adams’ reach.

Sebastien Pocognoli got his first Hampden win as Scotland boss but it was a nervy night

Although Ljupche Doriev worried Angus Gunn with a curling effort, Scotland began to exert some degree of control on the match. Lewis Ferguson kept the visitors hemmed in with a header into McTominay’s feet. The Napoli man saw his shot on the spin well saved by Stole Dimitrievski.

Pocognoli was frustrated when Slovakian referee Michal Ocenas blew for a foul on McTominay, his justifiable gripe being that playing an advantage would have seen Robertson have a crack at goal.

Dimitrievski had a decent night. Although Adams’ flashing header from McGinn’s corner took a deflection, a reflex save at his near post added to Scotland’s frustration.

North Macedonia were a spirited but ordinary side. They still had enough to thwart Pocognoli’s men.

Gannon-Doak saw plenty of the ball down the right, yet the end product often wasn’t there. The Bournemouth man did tee up Billy Gilmour for one dangerous cross. McTominay tried to replicate his iconic overhead kick against Denmark nearly a year ago. This time, his aim wasn’t true.

You could hardly blame Pocognoli’s star man for failing to find the net on that occasion.

Scott McTominay attempts an overhead spectacular a year on from THAT goal at Hampden

That wasn’t the case a few moments later when Adams slipped him in. Dimitrievski saved McTominay’s strike with an outstretched leg when he should have been picking the ball out of his net.

Adams had just blazed a strike high over the top while one-on-one with the keeper although the offside flag saved his blushes.

The visitors came closer to edging ahead when Eljif Elmas played the pass of the match over Scotland’s static defence to pick out Ezgjan Alioski. His lay-off was smashed into the side net by Enis Bardhi.

A wholly uninspiring first-half concluded with Robertson advancing up the left and launching a cross halfway to Castlemilk. This was not going well.

Pocognoli waited on the edge of the pitch for his players returning, his enthusiastic applause clearly audible in the arena.

His hopes of a breakthrough at the outset of the second period were dashed in extraordinary fashion. Adams did well to chase a ball down to the line and cut it back. McTominay and his marker couldn’t connect, leaving Gilmour the simple task of firing into an unguarded net. Leaning back, his failure to even hit the target was unfathomable.

Elmin Rastoder celebrates after silencing Hampden with a leveller for North Macedonia

Within seconds, the sense of relief inside Hampden was palpable as the opener finally arrived. Porteous got enough distance on his clearing header for Adams to barge Visar Musliu out of the way.

McGinn was alert to the situation and burst into the box. His crisp strike finally had the beating of the goalkeeper.

It should have settled Pocognoli’s side and paved the way for a comfortable result. Instead, they were pegged back within three minutes.

It was all just so simple and so avoidable. Bardhi’s whipped corner only needed McTominay to outjump his man. Flat-footed as the delivery arrived, he could only watch on in horror as Elmin Rastoder’s flashing header beat Angus Gunn.

Although Gilmour worked the keeper with a low strike, North Macedonia also sniffed a second goal. Time and time again, they got into pockets of space on the flanks and fired in dangerous crosses.

Adams made way for Oli McBurnie, the Hull man desperately hoping for his first goal on his 21st international appearance. He had a gilt-edged chance to get off the mark when rolled in by McGinn, but selflessly passed to the overlapping Gannon-Doak.

Scotland move on to their final game away in Switzerland as they look to finish on a high note

The winger appeared to take a heavy touch which allowed the keeper to rescue the situation. VAR, however, spotted that Dimitrievski had impeded him. Penalty.

McGinn did the necessary from 12 yards, smashing the ball straight down the middle for his 24th international goal.

North Macedonia, to their credit, kept going for it. They sensed a fragility in Scotland. Everyone in the ground could.

McGinn’s calm conversion proved to be just about enough to get the job done. But it’s fair to suggest that we are still awaiting lift-off in the new era.

SCOTLAND (3-4-1-2): Gunn; Porteous, Graham, Tierney; Gannon-Doak (Hickey 76), Ferguson, Gilmour (Christie 76), Robertson; McGinn; Adams (McBurnie 67), McTominay. Booked: Ferguson. Manager: Sebastien Pocognoli.

NORTH MACEDONIA (4-2-3-1): Dimitrievski; Ilievski, Mladenovski, Musliu, Alioski; Gashtarov (Elezi 64), Elmas (Stankovski 78); Churlinov (Maleski 64), Bardhi, Doriev (Nikolov 85); Rastoder. Booked: None. Manager: Goce Sedloski.

#2012. PM: Hojbjerg still an option for Milan – January move possible thanks to €15m price tag

AC Milan are reportedly interested in making a move for Pierre-Emile Hojbjerg when the January mercato opens, it seems.

There have been suggestions about a move for Hojbjerg for some time, and Milan could attempt a move in January, especially if Christian Comotto departs on loan. The Dane, according to PianetaMilan, is still an option for January if another midfielder is to arrive.

Of course, Luka Modric’s likely retirement at the end of the season will give the Rossoneri time to think about his replacement, or even replacements, and Hojbjerg could be a new tool for Ruben Amorim.

#2011. Inside Boreham Wood, the only unbeaten team in England's top seven tiers: Boss LUKE GARRARD explains how play-off heartache and a 'genius' owner are fuelling his swashbuckling side's promotion bid

Published: 21:00 EST, 12 November 2026 | Updated: 17:17 EST, 13 November 2026

Of 252 clubs in the top seven tiers of English football, the last one unbeaten can be found in the pristine confines of Meadow Park, yards from the studios where the Indiana Jones adventures were filmed.

Boreham Wood are on their own crusade. And the Holy Grail is a long-coveted place in the EFL for the runaway leaders of the National League. They have 44 points from 16 games with 44 goals and are 12 points clear ahead of a trip to Yeovil on Saturday, finding success with a distinct passing style.

In a remarkable 4-3 comeback win against Hartlepool earlier this month, Luke Garrard's team made 1,022 passes, beating the Premier League record of 1,015 set by Manchester City against Swansea in April 2018.

The electric start to this campaign is, according to Garrard, fuelled by the lingering pain of defeat in the play-off final at Wembley in May when they conceded an equaliser in the seventh minute of stoppage time and lost on penalties.

'That broke me mentally for four or five days,' the Wood boss tells Daily Mail Sport. 'I reflected hugely and had a long, hard look at myself because I could not walk back for the first day of pre-season without the energy and heart for the job.

'I spoke to the owners and the staff about the first meeting I wanted to have when we came back in. It involved everyone at the club, and it was a message to tell all of them that as much as it hurt us, we needed to use the hurt as our fuel and our driving force.

'We got quite lucky getting some results on the board quite quickly and that builds momentum and belief.'

National League leaders Boreham Wood, under the guidance of their manager Luke Garrard, are the last unbeaten team in the top seven tiers of English football

Boreham Wood are a slick operation, skilfully run despite crowds seldom breaking 1,500. They share Meadow Park with Arsenal Women and Arsenal Under 21s and U18s

Boreham Wood are a slick operation, skilfully run despite crowds seldom breaking 1,500 by chairman Danny Hunter and his son Charlie, who is the sporting director and in charge of recruitment strategy. They are punching above their weight with a mid-table budget.

Hunter senior is a former props master in the film industry who worked at the nearby Elstree Studios among others, and whose father Mickey was a double promotion winning manager of club in the 1970s.

He took control in 1999 and has overseen investment of more than £14million and the rise from the depths of the Isthmian League to the brink of the EFL, forging effective relationships with local authorities and Premier League neighbours Arsenal, who use Meadow Park for their Women, Under-21 and Under-18 teams.

Arsenal ad boards surround an immaculate pitch, and work is underway at the venue on a £4m project to create a covered South Stand terrace incorporating improved 'Fan Zone' style facilities for away fans and a new first-team building.

Garrard's team train in the mornings on the artificial pitches beside the stadium, which are available for community use in the evenings and home in the afternoons to the club's academy.

Manchester City's Iliman Ndiaye and Hull's Sorba Thomas were both nurtured as young players at Boreham Wood. So was Abdul Abdulmalik, a 23-year-old winger signed after his release from Millwall in 2024 and sold to Djurgardens in Sweden for £1.5m in August.

The Abdulmalik fee shattered the non-League record set when Fleetwood Town sold Jamie Vardy to Leicester in 2012.

There was an untidy episode towards the end of the transfer window when Abdulmalik went public to plead for a move, but the Hunters secured an enviable price for their star and in another example of their good housekeeping have yet to reinvest the money in the team. It is still there as a war chest as they target promotion.

Abdul Abdulmalik, a 23-year-old winger signed after his release from Millwall in 2024, was sold to Djurgardens in Sweden for £1.5million in August

The club is run by chairman Danny Hunter (pictured) and his son Charlie, who is the sporting director. Hunter Snr is a former props master in the film industry

The windfall from Wood's famous FA Cup run in 2021-22 was invested into refitting the interiors of the ground including the dressing rooms and swish hospitality areas recognised among the best in non-League.

Meadow Park has a bar bedecked with souvenirs from those games and named in honour of Mark Ricketts, scorer of the goal to beat Bournemouth, who were at the time bound for promotion to the Premier League, and which clinched a date with Everton in the fifth round at Goodison Park.

'At no stage has the chairman given me any pressure to generate money from prize funds and cup runs,' says 41-year-old Garrard. 'It's only ever been about creating moments and memories.

'He (Hunter) is a Boreham Wood boy through and through and it's always been his greatest wish to lead the club into the EFL. He wants to leave a legacy. I adore him, I think he's a genius. We have a great working relationship. I do not take for granted the luxury of being manager here, especially after losing my job two years ago.'

Garrard has a long association with the club. First as a player, briefly in 2005 and then returning for a second spell four years later, a loan move from Wimbledon which became permanent and led him into his first coaching roles and the manager's job.

He took control in 2015 with the Wood in the top tier of non-League for the first time. Three times they reached the play-offs without promotion and there were many highs including Goodison before Garrard's tearful exit after relegation in April 2024, only for him to be back in charge by September.

During five months away, he turned down interest from one club because it took him too far from his family home and received two direct and sobering rejections from National League clubs. Feedback from the first told him he 'wasn't on the list and never would be' and from the second that he 'wasn't good enough' for them.

Perhaps it reveals some of football's inherent petty-mindedness towards Boreham Wood. They are perceived by some as upstarts with limited history and small crowds, putting the noses of 'bigger' clubs out of joint with the streamlined success of their business model and Hunter's backing, like a non-League version of Bournemouth or Brentford.

They have been known to charge scouts for tickets and charge away teams to broadcast, which some refuse to do on a point of principle. For a time, they had a reputation for pragmatic and unattractive football – but not any longer.

Garrard was rejected by two National League clubs and found himself back at Boreham Wood. 'The stars aligned,' as he puts it

Prolific striker Matt Rush has is fuelling Boreham Wood's promotion push

Garrard was probably entitled to have expected more interest in his services. Instead, he spent two days following the second of those rejections in earnest conversation with his wife about the need to look for work away from football when out of the blue came a call from Boreham Wood.

Within another two days he was back in his old job. 'The stars aligned,' as he puts it. 'It was the best team in the National South with the best players, the best facilities and the best budget. I had to go and deliver.'

And he did. With promotion back to the National League at the first attempt. Then the near-miss heartache of Wembley. Now this early-season surge thanks in part to the goals of striker Matt Rush. The Wood seem to have emerged stronger despite selling their most talented individual, which is a reassuring situation for any coach.

Unbeaten since April in the National League, they scored 25 goals in seven games in October and League One Wigan became the first team to beat them in any competition this season, in the FA Cup first round on Saturday.

It could yet prove a blessing in Boreham Wood's quest for the Holy Grail.

#2009. Paul McStay on refusing Celtic autobiography request and saying ‘polite no thanks’ to Rangers

The Paul McStay paradox has been a feature of Scottish football for many years. Although his name continues to be sung at nearly every Celtic game, the man himself has been one of the least visible former players of the modern era.

He was an elegant presence in the centre of the Parkhead side’s midfield for almost all the 1980s and a good chunk of the 1990s, albeit injury dogged him in the later stages of his magnificent one-club career. A clip of a podcast he recorded with former teammate Brian McClair recently caught the eye, as it also featured a remarkably well-preserved copy of an old Edinburgh-based music newspaper called Cut.

Did you know with a Digital Subscription to The Scotsman, you can get unlimited access to the website including our premium content, as well as benefiting from fewer ads, loyalty rewards and much more.

An equally well preserved McStay, now 62, and McClair discussed featuring on the wrap around front cover of the February 1987 edition. Pat Nevin was not the only thinking man’s footballer at the time. Now based in Australia, which might account for McStay’s healthy radiance as well as the infrequent appearances, all of this must feel like another lifetime ago.

So why has it taken him so long to publish his memoirs? That is itself a long story and is one of the reasons why McStay, whose family has playing ties to Celtic dating back to the 1920s, is launching his long-awaited autobiography at the home of …….Queen’s Park Football Club.

It was originally meant to be launched at the slightly more appropriate Celtic Park last year, while on a trip home to raise the title flag before the opening league game against St Mirren. “It didn’t work out that way,” he explains. “Basically the club sent an agreement for them to sign off on the book.”

Celtic were unhappy with some parts, probably related to the vexed matter of his eventual exit in 1997 after 16 years of stellar, some might even say genius, service.

The upshot is McStay has published his own book on his own terms. “I’m doing it independently, doing it on my own,” he says. “And I have been quite honest. It’s my book, my story, my life. So I just said I couldn’t sign the agreement. I’ll do my own thing.”

If the club’s mantra is let the people sing then surely allowing former players, especially such loyal servants as McStay, to tell their own story should be taken as read. “I just thought: No, I can’t have that,” he says.

McStay was sent off just once (at Dens Park in a 1994 League Cup tie v Dundee) and was described by Alex Ferguson, after his testimonial against Manchester United in 1995, as the “ultimate professional”. He was also awarded an MBE by the Queen and picked it up from Her Majesty herself in 1997 at Holyrood Palace. Happily married to Ann Marie, with whom he has six children, he is one of the most uncontroversial players ever to play the game. He nevertheless makes for ravishingly good copy.

“I’ve just got to tell my story,” McStay says. “If people are not aware of that, that's why I'm happy to share it. I just felt it was time to put how I lived it and my perception about certain things that happened as well, and put it in black and white.”

One regrettable consequence of the delay in his story getting out there is that we have been denied knowledge of a transfer tale to end nearly all transfer tales. Never mind music magazines, McStay would have featured on the front page of every newspaper in the land if the then Celtic skipper had joined Rangers in 1992.

The Ibrox club were buying nearly everyone else, including Mo Johnston in 1989, during this era, so why not make a play for the best player at their biggest rivals? The religion thing had already been put to bed with Johnston…..ahem. Manager Walter Smith made the cheeky enquiry through a mutual contact.

“That was a question put to me in ’92, yes,” confirms McStay, who includes this startling snippet in Maestro: The Paul McStay Autobiography. “It was a polite ‘no thanks’. I think that’s the best way of putting it.”

He is sworn to secrecy on the identity of who was sent by Smith to sound him out. “I can't say,” he says. “But I know he's a friend of Walter. I never spoke to Walter about it.” His relationship with the Rangers legend dated back to their involvement in Scotland youth teams, Smith as the budding coach and McStay one of the country’s brightest young hopes. “When you talk about mentors and things like that, Walter was up there,” he says. “Andy Roxburgh was youth team manager in ’82 when we won the Euros and Walter was part of that. Since then, there’s always been a bond. He is a wonderful man and obviously, he did well at Rangers, which had an effect on me. But as a person, I got on really well with Walter.”

The phrase ‘had an effect on me’ is a wonderful way of saying McStay, towards the end of his Celtic career, seemed perpetually pitted in an almost one-man battle to stop Rangers winning nine-in-a-row. It was unfair to him, just as the financial imbalance - McStay has a few things to say about Rangers' spending power in his book - was unfair for the rest of Scottish football.

Aberdeen rather than Celtic came closest to stopping the Ibrox side’s march. McStay endured six trophyless years between 1989 and an emotional Scottish Cup win under Tommy Burns in 1995.

Not long afterwards, reeling from an X-ray report confirming the “virtual obliteration” of part of his ankle joint, McStay accepted that he had to consider retirement. But intense rehabilitation work saw him make another return, although he was clearly toiling. He finally called it a day at the end of the 1996-97 season. The then owner Fergus McCann, along with others, helped make this already difficult decision a horrendous experience. He was given the feeling that Celtic thought he was “bluffing” about the injury in a bid to negotiate a new deal with another club.

“The exit wasn't great,” he says, understating things hugely. "I never ever thought I'd leave Celtic in that way. There were a lot of good times along the way, as well as ups and downs…

"But to me, it was very important to get that message out about how it ended. Because even at that time, there was a bit of PR coming out about certain things. And it wasn't quite accurate. I don't know what the club will feel about that. But I've got to tell the story the way it happened. And that's it.”

Encouraged by Tommy Burns, he gained his coaching certificates and applied for the Under-16 Academy coach’s position at Celtic during Martin O’Neill’s first stint in charge. However, former teammate Jim McInally got the job instead. Australia beckoned in 2010.

“I do enjoy the element of being able to hide away, out of the road,” he says. It must have been comforting to know that across the other side of the world, every time Celtic played, his name was being sung in the chorus of the stirring “Willie Maley” song, which will be familiar to nearly everyone who watches football in Scotland: “And they gave us James McGrory and Paul McStay….” It’s a paean to storied past, one McStay is an integral part of.

“That started when I stopped playing,” he says. “James McStay was actually in the original song and then, through time, the younger generations changed it to Paul.” Every day’s a school day in the company of a Maestro.

Paul McStay was speaking at the launch of his autobiography Maestro. To purchase copies of the Celtic legend's book go to paulmcstay.com.

#2008. Rangers seek January reunion for Ibrox favourite as update emerges on forgotten £4.5million man

Rangers are ready to reignite their interest in former fan favourite Vaclav Cerny, with Besiktas reportedly ready to let him leave in January.

According to reports, Rangers manager Derek McInnes showed interest in the winger during the summer transfer window, and the Glasgow giants reportedly held discussions with his club to bring the Czech international back to Ibrox permanently.

Did you know with a Digital Subscription to The Scotsman, you can get unlimited access to the website including our premium content, as well as benefiting from fewer ads, loyalty rewards and much more.

Those talks are understood to have broken down over Besiktas’ asking price. However, Rangers are ready to return to the negotiating table when the transfer window reopens, with reports claiming the club now believes that he could be made available in January after failing to impress in Istanbul this season.

Cerny, 29, spent a successful season on loan at Rangers during the 2024/25 campaign, notching 18 goals and assisting a further nine across all competitions after being signed by Philippe Clement from Wolfsburg that summer. However, a permanent deal didn’t materialise, as the club changed ownership and named Russell Martin as the club’s new head coach.

After leaving Rangers, he moved to the Turkish Super League instead, and performed admirably in his debut campaign at the Tupras Stadium, registering 15 goal contributions as Besiktas finished fourth. However, he hasn’t replicated that form so far this term, last scoring in a 4-1 win over Marseille in the Europa League back on September 17.

Meanwhile, on-loan Rangers winger Oscar Cortes looks set to return to the club in the new year, with reports claiming Huracan have turned down their option to make the deal permanent at the end of the Argentinian season, which is scheduled to end in December.

Cortes, 22, originally signed for Rangers on loan from Ligue 1 outfit RC Lens in February 2024, scoring once and assisting twice in his first seven appearances, before injury ended his season. After joining permanently for £4.5million at the end of the campaign, the Colombian’s injury troubles followed him into the new season, and he missed several games after developing a knee injury in the 0-0 draw with Hearts on opening day.

Dogged by various issues throughout his first full season at Ibrox, he made just 10 starts and was allowed to sign on loan for Spanish second tier side Sporting Gijon. He struggled in Spain, though, failing to score in eight appearances, and had his loan cut short before moving to Huracan on a similar deal.

His stint at Buenos Aires has been more successful, though. A regular in the Huracan starting XI, he has registered nine goal contributions across the season. However, despite his strong form, reports in South America say he will be allowed to return to Govan when their season ends next month, with Huracan unable to pay the Ibrox side's asking price of around £4.2million.

The fee has also scared off Atletico Nacional, who were mulling over a deal to bring him back to Colombia recently, with the club understood to have cooled their interest over Rangers’ asking price for Cortes.

Former Celtic managerial target Robbie Keane has been tipped for a surprise return to the dugout after being named a major favourite for a top EFL Championship job, with ex-Rangers and Hibs bosses also in the running.

Keane, 46, was believed to have held talks with the Celtic hierarchy over becoming the club’s new manager in the summer. Out of work since quitting his role as head coach of the Hungarian side in May, the former Republic of Ireland international is now one of the leading favourites to take over at promotion-chasing side Swansea City following Vitor Matos’ decision to depart to become the new manager of Ligue 1 side Strasbourg on Tuesday.

Currently sixth in the EFL Championship table, Swansea signed former Scottish Premiership trio Stephen Welsh, Elijah Just and Ross Stewart in the summer, and had started strongly under Matos. However, despite being just three points off the automatic promotion places, the Portuguese manager opted to leave for Stade de la Meinau.

While former Mainz manager Bo Henriksen is the current 5/1 favourite, Keane is joint-third on the list alongside recently sacked Manchester United boss, Michael Carrick, at 14/1. Ex-Middlesbrough and Wolverhampton Wanderers manager Rob Edwards is priced at 10/1.

Former Rangers boss Russell Martin is also among the candidates, with the current Leicester City boss having an outside chance of a sensational return to the club that he left in the summer of 2023. Appointed as head coach of Swansea in August 2021, the 40-year-old won 39 of his 99 games in charge of the club before being poached by Southampton, where he led the club to promotion via the EFL Championship playoffs.

Even more interestingly, former Hibs head coach Paul Heckingbottom is named on the list of favourites following his sacking at Preston North End in September. The 49-year-old endured a tough eight-month spell in charge at Easter Road in 2019, but went on to achieve automatic promotion to the English Premier League in his next role with Sheffield United.

After leaving the Blades, he spent two seasons at Deepdale, but was relieved of his duties earlier this season after losing six of his first seven games. #2006. Former Rangers boss breaks silence on troubled 177-day reign with emotional ‘true friends’ statement

Former Rangers and Sunderland head coach Michael Beale has broken his silence on his turbulent 177-day spell in charge of Belgian Pro League side Zulte Waregem after resigning last week.

Beale, 46, brought down the curtain on his short time at the Elindus Arena following the 4-1 defeat to Sint-Truidense last week, which made it six consecutive league defeats. Their worst run of results since October 7, 2018, they are just four points above the relegation zone.

Did you know with a Digital Subscription to The Scotsman, you can get unlimited access to the website including our premium content, as well as benefiting from fewer ads, loyalty rewards and much more.

His spell in Belgium was plagued by rumours of a breakdown in his relationship with senior figures at the club over Waregem’s direction and strategy. Beale actually started the campaign brightly, going unbeaten in their opening five games. However, their form quickly deteriorated, and they have failed to register a victory since September 6.

His first managerial role since being sacked after just 12 games in charge at Sunderland almost three years ago, he exited Waregem with an identical record to the one he held at the Stadium of Light, with four wins, two draws, and six losses, meaning he left both sides with a 33.3% win rate after 12 games.

In a short statement confirming his departure, Waregem said: “After several internal discussions between the head coach and the club, both parties decided to end their collaboration by mutual agreement.” Zulte Waregem are yet to appoint Beale’s permanent successor, with interim head coach Steve Colpaert expected to take charge of their league game vs Royal Antwerp at the weekend.

A week on from his departure, Beale penned an emotional farewell message to Waregem via his official Instagram page, writing: “Waregem, thankyou. It has been an honour and privilege to manage this club and I want to begin by thanking the fans for their incredible support. From day one, your passion and loyalty stood out and made coaching this club feel truly special. I will never forget the welcome you gave me and I have been overwhelmed by all your messages and kind words over the last few days.

“This community has become a home to me and to everyone I met in the local shops, coffee houses, parks, restaurants and bars: thank you. Many of you have become true friends and you have made me feel completely one of your own. I also want to show my gratitude to the players and staff for their hard work, dedication and the special memories we created together. You have been a pleasure to work with and I wish you every success in the future.”

The ex-Rangers manager first joined Rangers as first-team coach during Steven Gerrard’s spell as manager at Ibrox. However, he left to join the former Liverpool icon in a similar role when he was appointed at Aston Villa in November 2021. Shortly afterwards, Beale took on his first managerial role with Queens Park Rangers.

He lasted just six months at Loftus Road before being poached by Rangers as a replacement for Giovanni van Bronckhorst. He struggled in the main role at Rangers, though, and was sacked in October 2023 before joining Sunderland three months later.

#2005. Chelsea are great entertainers but possess clear weakness

Chelsea are promising to be this season’s Premier League entertainers and yet manager Xabi Alonso seemingly believes less is more when it comes to possession.

Alonso has started with two wins from two league games in charge of Chelsea, with his team scoring seven goals and conceding five. So far, it has been a lot of fun – if not entirely convincing.

But perhaps the most significant numbers are around how much – or how little – Chelsea are having the ball. Having finished their 3-2 victory over Fulham with 38.11 per cent of possession, Chelsea had just 25.6 per cent in the 4-3 success over Brighton and Hove Albion and successfully completed 146 passes. Both were their lowest figures on record in the Premier League.

“The data is not important,” Alonso said. “It’s how you play and what we can do better. I don’t say ‘today we need to have 60 per cent or 20 per cent’. I never talk about those things. It’s about how to prepare, how to be more competitive.”

Chelsea’s third goal against Brighton, scored in the 32nd minute, best summed up the London club under Alonso to date. It took the home side three passes to go from the edge of their own penalty area to João Pedro scoring against his former club.

Jorrel Hato passed the ball to Morgan Rogers, he then released Hato down the left and the wing-back slid the ball across for João Pedro to finish. It was a devastating counter-attack and should have put Chelsea on course for a much easier win.

Joao Pedro finishes off a deadly Chelsea counter-attack and gives the Blues a 3-0 lead 🔥 pic.twitter.com/wAr0ckIgXJ

“After 30 minutes, we are 3-0 and probably, in that moment, we have played too much the result,” Alonso said. “It’s quite normal, it happens in many teams. I am sure in the future we can manage it better.”

It is one thing outscoring Fulham and a depleted Brighton team without having the ball, but can Chelsea do that against the bigger and better teams? We will get an early indicator in the next game against Arsenal at the Emirates.

Alonso’s approach has some similarities to the way in which Antonio Conte set up his Chelsea title-winning team. Just as Conte converted Victor Moses into an effective right wing-back, Alonso started Pedro Neto there on Sunday.

After Roméo Lavia had opened the scoring, it was Neto who grabbed Chelsea’s second goal against Brighton by drifting into the penalty area to finish from Rogers’s low cross.

"It's a nightmare for the goalkeeper!"Bart Verbruggen and Mats Wieffer's collision leads to Romeo Lavia scoring his first goal for Chelsea ⚽️ pic.twitter.com/q5awbdwVV0

"Pedro Neto Pounces!"Morgan Rogers goes past his defender before sliding the ball across to Neto! 💥 pic.twitter.com/WHZCIGsOLl

But whereas Conte’s team gave up little at the back, Alonso’s Chelsea are yet to balance their effective transitional play with shutting out their opponents.

Neto was partly to blame for Brighton’s first goal, as he missed a challenge in the build-up to Malick Yalcouyé’s brilliant volley. Making his Chelsea debut, goalkeeper Emiliano Martínez could do nothing to stop it and can expect to be kept busy this season if things do not change.

“I have come here to challenge and to try and win the Premier League,” Martínez said. “I know the talent we have up front. I try to bring that solidity at the back.”

"Yalcouye with a sumptuous volley!"Malick Yalcouye puts Brighton on the scoreboard with a venomous volley 😳 pic.twitter.com/8UeeyvPjUw

Conte’s Chelsea had N’Golo Kanté to mop up in midfield and that is an area of the pitch that is causing Alonso some difficulties. Manchester City target Enzo Fernández was once again left out of the squad and Moisés Caicedo was not deemed fit enough to start.

Caicedo was eventually thrown on when Chelsea were trying to stop Brighton completing a remarkable comeback, but he was quickly forced off again with an injury. The club have been exploring a move for Monaco midfielder Lamine Camara and that need looks even more pressing now.

“We want the best for the team and that’s why we took a decision [on Fernández] against Luton and today,” Alonso said. “What’s going to develop? We’re not sure. We can prepare. We are preparing for all the scenarios. But I assure you that whatever happens, from Wednesday [when the transfer window is shut] we’ll have a good enough squad to compete in all the Premier League games.”

Chelsea’s new set-piece coach Austin MacPhee had celebrated Lavia’s goal, which came partly as a result of a corner but owed more to a mistake from Brighton goalkeeper Bart Verbruggen.

MacPhee, however, will not have liked Brighton’s second-half goals. It was from a short corner that the visitors managed to work the ball to Pascal Gross and his cross was diverted into his own net by João Pedro.

Joao Pedro puts Pascal Groß's cross into his own net and Brighton have brought it back to 3-2 👀 pic.twitter.com/maBMwVu3DC

Gross’s headed third goal also came at the end of a set-piece, but, fortunately for Chelsea, it was in the sixth minute of added time and Cole Palmer had already made the points safe for the home team before then.

Palmer had done little to impress watching England head coach Thomas Tuchel until he picked up the ball in the 74th minute, shrugged off two Brighton challenges and produced a brilliant finish to beat Verbruggen.

Cole Palmer finishes EXPERTLY to give Chelsea their two-goal cushion back 💥 pic.twitter.com/6xI9W8xe2q

Fabian Hürzeler, the Brighton manager, said his team “dominated” the game, but acknowledged: “I think if you spend so much money on these kinds of players, like Rogers, Palmer or João [Pedro], then, of course, a team like Chelsea can rely on this individual quality. And they showed it in certain moments of the game.”

Palmer, João Pedro and Rogers are clearly going to be a huge problem for Chelsea’s opponents. But Alonso’s team cannot rely on having to score three or four goals to win games. And they might need to have a bit more of the ball.

"The game today was a special game for me." João Pedro says he was happy with his performance for Chelsea against Brighton 🔵 pic.twitter.com/fWSqWo7ert

6 - João Pedro today was the sixth player (and first for Chelsea) to score a goal, assist a goal, and score an own goal in the same Premier League game, and first since Tottenham Hotspur's Son Heung-min against Man City in December 2023.Eventful. pic.twitter.com/xRVjqkOY9D

There is no time for Brighton to push for the equaliser as the final whistle is blown at Stamford Bridge. Chelsea make it two wins from two to start the new Premier League season but were pushed all the way by Brighton. It finishes 4-3 at Stamford Bridge.

It could well be the last touch of the game but Brighton have a small amount of hope as Gross heads past Martinez. If that had come a few minutes ago, maybe Brighton could have pushed for a draw.

Brighton have a corner and if they are to have any chance of potentially rescuing a point, they have to score right now. De Cuyper’s inswinger is clipped into a dangerous area but for some odd reason referee Michael Oliver gives Chelsea a free-kick. Absolutely ridiculous decision; there was no foul in any way, shape or form.

Chelsea look to counter through Pedro, who is then brought down by Costinha. It is an easy booking for referee Michael Oliver to give.

How many added minutes will there be? The answer is five minutes.

Boscagli is booked for bringing down Rogers.

This is a concern for Chelsea as Caicedo, who came on as a second-half substitute, is now having to go off injured. In his place is former Brighton man Barco, who slapped Bellingham at the World Cup. Barco is booed vociferously by the travelling Brighton fans.

Meanwhile Leeds are level 1-1 against Brentford at Elland Road thanks to Calvert-Lewin’s equaliser.

Double change for Brighton as Costinha and David replace Wieffer and Kostoulas.

Brighton scored four a week ago against Aston Villa on the opening weekend but have conceded four this weekend. If they can get a goal though soon, it would make the home fans inside Stamford Bridge very nervous.

Kadioglu has an effort from the edge of the Chelsea box but drags his effort wide.

Meanwhile, up in the north east, Isidor has put Sunderland 1-0 up against Fulham at the Stadium of Light.

Palmer has been pretty quiet today but Chelsea’s two-goal lead is restored. He receives it from Pedro and drives forward through the Brighton half. As he approaches the edge of the penalty area, Palmer calmly slots home into the bottom corner.

Cole Palmer finishes EXPERTLY to give Chelsea their two-goal cushion back 💥 pic.twitter.com/6xI9W8xe2q

Tuchel will have like that. He may not have had a brilliant game, but Palmer just scored a brilliant goal. That should be enough for Chelsea.

Fabian Hurzeler turns to his bench for the first time today as Osman comes on for Yalcouye, who was impressive.

Xabi Alonso turns to his bench again as Chavarria replaces Colwill.

We have this news from the Premier League:

#CHEBHAMatch Officials are operating in the second half without communications packs due to an ongoing technical issue. VAR remains in operation via a back-up system using messages sent to the referee's watch and radio communication to the fourth official if required.

Dunk is in trouble. The ball is played forward by Gusto down the right channel to pick out the run of Pedro into the Brighton half. Dunk brings Pedro down but is fortunate that Vuskovic was covering so that is why there is no red card. Dunk is rightly booked.

Chelsea are on the ropes at the moment and Brighton can sense another goal. Boscagli is the latest Brighton player to have an effort and Martinez is forced into a decent save down to his left.

Xabi Alonso is going to respond to the Brighton momentum with a triple change. James, Acheampong and Caicedo replace Neto, Lavia and Fofana.

It is all Brighton and Chelsea are seriously wobbling. Gomez has his fourth chance of the second half and is not far off scoring as his effort hits the side netting. You can sense the anxiety inside Stamford Bridge and it is the travelling Brighton fans making all the noise.

This game is well and truly back on. Chelsea looked in complete control at 3-0 up but now there is just one goal in it. Brighton work a corner short and appear to have wasted the chance but Yalcouye slides a wonderful pass into the right side of the box to pick out the run of Gross, whose shot/cross takes a big deflection off former Brighton man Pedro and goes past Martinez into the Chelsea net.

Joao Pedro puts Pascal Groß's cross into his own net and Brighton have brought it back to 3-2 👀 pic.twitter.com/maBMwVu3DC

Gomez has already missed two chances in this second half and he now has his third opportunity since the break. His powerful effort from the right side of the box forces Martinez into a decent save at his near post...

England head coach Thomas Tuchel is at Stamford Bridge today. He won’t have like Cole Palmer’s miss much and Palmer is probably the only Chelsea attacking player not to have impressed so far. There’s still time, though.

Chelsea have two big chances to score a fourth but cannot take either. First, Neto takes advantage of poor defending from Kadioglu and has a shot saved at the near post by Verbruggen. Then Palmer has a glorious opportunity inside the six-yard box from Rogers’ cross but somehow Palmer guides it over the bar. I am going to say it now that I do not think we have seen an end to the goals today.

Fofana is rightly booked for an earlier challenge on De Cuyper as he completely took him out and Brighton now have a free-kick deep into the Chelsea half after a foul by Neto.

Boscagli clips a lovely free-kick to the back post, where he perfectly picks out Gomez, who has a free header from the edge of the six-yard box but his powerful header goes wide of the far post. That should have been a goal and that is a mighty let-off for Chelsea.

Gomez has a decent chance for Brighton on the edge of the Chelsea penalty area but he fires his effort well wide.

Chelsea attack from back to front, with Martinez launching a long ball forward from inside his own box to pick out the run of Pedro into the Brighton half. Pedro ends up having a shot blocked inside the Brighton penalty area.

Palmer was very influential for Chelsea at Fulham on Monday night and, despite Chelsea scoring three first-half goals, he has been quiet today.

We are back under way at Stamford Bridge. Despite Chelsea being two goals ahead, it does not feel like Brighton are out of this one.

Chelsea 3 Brighton 1Leeds 0 Brentford 1Sunderland 0 Fulham 0

Possession: Chelsea 29%-71% BrightonShots: 9-6Shots on target: 4-3Corners: 2-4Touches in opposition box: 15-10

Chelsea go in 3-1 at half-time, having only had 29.3 per cent of possession. They finished with about 35 per cent possession in the 3-2 victory over Fulham, so it seems Alonso is setting his team up very much as a counter-attacking side. It’s all very Antonio Conte.

Vuskovic has a late effort in the first half from range and it goes just over Martinez’s bar.

The first half is then brought to an end not long after and Chelsea take a 3-1 lead into the break.

The Brighton fans enjoy an audacious Pedro backheel that does not come off. Moments later, Gross clips in a cross from the right that picks out Gomez in the box but his header goes over the bar.

There will be two added minutes at the end of this first half.

There has been a goal in one of the other 2pm kick-offs. At Elland Road, Brentford, who were one of the most impressive teams on the opening weekend, have taken the lead over Leeds through Schade.

After a dreadful clearance from Dunk, Rogers shoots from just outside the box but it goes wide of Verbruggen’s left post.

Pedro has a shot blocked inside the Brighton area before Rogers also has an effort blocked.

At 3-0 down, they looked down and out but maybe the visitors have a route back into the game. Kostoulas is denied by Martinez before the ball comes to Yalcouye, who volleys first time. His emphatic effort smashes off the inside of the far post and into the net. A fine way to score your first Premier League goal and maybe this game is not over quite yet.

"Yalcouye with a sumptuous volley!"Malick Yalcouye puts Brighton on the scoreboard with a venomous volley 😳 pic.twitter.com/8UeeyvPjUw

There have already been three goals in the first half at Stamford Bridge but it is still goalless at Elland Road and the Stadium of Light in the other two 2pm kick-offs.

The Brighton fans have been singing ‘The Falklands are ours’ at Chelsea’s Argentine substitute Valentin Barco. Barco was part of the Argentina squad who celebrated his nation’s World Cup win over England by displaying a Falklands banner. The Brighton fans had also been giving the club’s former striker Joao Pedro some stick. Pedro celebrated his goal right in front of them. Touche.

The Brazilian missed a sitter earlier but he makes no mistake this time and goes to celebrate in front of the travelling Brighton fans. Pedro owes a lot of gratitude from Hato, who drives down Chelsea’s left from inside his own half to the edge of the Brighton box. The Dutchman passes to his left to find Pedro, who takes one touch before clinically slotting home into the far corner. Is that game, set and match?

Joao Pedro finishes off a deadly Chelsea counter-attack and gives the Blues a 3-0 lead 🔥 pic.twitter.com/wAr0ckIgXJ

Brighton have their first real sighter on goal. Gomez clips in a lovely delivery to the far post to pick out the run of Yalcouye into the box. Yalcouye gets to it on the stretch and his effort is straight at Martinez.

Brighton have had 70% possession but their xG currently sits at 0.03. Despite having a lot of the ball, they really have not looked like scoring. You do though have to bear in mind that they are without forwards like Minteh, Rutter and Mitoma due to injury. Will Minteh still be a Brighton player when the window shuts?

How has Pedro missed? The former Brighton man absolutely should have put Chelsea 3-0 up and that could have been game, set and match. The ball is played in behind down the right channel and Neto outmuscles Kadioglu, who goes to ground near the byline. Neto then unselfishly from the right side of the box squares it for Pedro, who takes a few touches before getting his shot away. It seems harder to miss than to score but somehow puts his effort wide of the far post.

After Martinez easily catches a corner from Gross, the Chelsea fans start singing the name of their new goalkeeper.

Brighton are dominating posession but are yet to have a shot. Chelsea meanwhile have had three shots, all on target, and have scored twice.

The hosts have their second inside the opening quarter of an hour. Rogers does well on the left side of the box to hold off Vuskovic before squaring the ball. Neto runs across Kadioglu’s blindside and pokes home first time from eight yards out. Kadioglu should really have dealt with that and was too flat-footed. He should not have allowed Neto to get to that ball first.

"Pedro Neto Pounces!"Morgan Rogers goes past his defender before sliding the ball across to Neto! 💥 pic.twitter.com/WHZCIGsOLl

The travelling Brighton fans are making sure that Pedro knows what they think of their former player.

Up in the stands, England boss Thomas Tuchel is sat next to Brazil manager Carlo Ancelotti, both former Chelsea bosses.

Since the start of the 2024/25 season, no goalkeeper in the Premier League has made more errors leading to goals than Verbruggen’s 10. Second on that list; Sanchez, who is not in the Chelsea squad today.

Brighton win their first corner of the afternoon and Martinez is forced into action, punching away at his near post as the delivery threatened to creep in.

That is an absolute gift for the home side after a huge error from Brighton. Pedro flicks on at the near post and Wieffer makes the block near his own line. Verbruggen then tries to catch the loose ball but he and Wieffer end up getting into each others’ way. The ball then falls to Lavia, who pokes home. As they did at Craven Cottage the other night, Chelsea hit the front early.

"It's a nightmare for the goalkeeper!"Bart Verbruggen and Mats Wieffer's collision leads to Romeo Lavia scoring his first goal for Chelsea ⚽️ pic.twitter.com/q5awbdwVV0

There was a fist pump from Chelsea’s new set-piece coach Austin MacPhee after Romeo Lavia’s goal from the corner. It looks like MacPhee will be claiming credit for that one, even though it came thanks to an error from Brighton goalkeeper Bart Verbruggen. Xabi Alonso also celebrated with MacPhee.

Chelsea win the first corner of the afternoon after Dunk blocked Neto’s cross...

He might be trying to sell his shares in Chelsea, but co-owner Todd Boehly is at today’s game in the Stamford Bridge stands.

Before we get going, Stamford Bridge pays tribute to Bobby Tambling and Ken Bates, who both died over the summer. Wreaths are laid in their memory with their families carrying framed pictures of the two men.

Both sides emerge from the tunnel at Stamford Bridge and we are moments away from kick-off in west London. Here is a reminder of how the two sides line up this afternoon:

Chelsea: Martinez, Fofana, Lacroix, Colwill, Neto, Gusto, Lavia, Hato, Palmer, Rogers, Joao Pedro.Substitutes: Penders, James, Acheampong, Chavarria, Caicedo, Barco, Gittens, Estevao, Welbeck.

Brighton: Verbruggen, Wieffer, Boscagli, Dunk, Vuskovic, Gross, Gomez, De Cuyper, Kadioglu, Yalcouye, Kostoulas.Substitutes: Steele, Struijk, Hadjam, Promise, Osman, Costinha, Cozier-Duberry, O’Riley, Oriola.

As you’d expect, there were big cheers for Emi Martinez from the Chelsea fans ahead of kick-off. He responded by shaking a fist in the air and giving them a big round of applause. This is his first game since the World Cup final for Argentina.

Chelsea had gone 77 League games without fielding a player aged 30 plus before handing goalkeeper Emi Martinez a debut today. The Argentine celebrates his 34th birthday on September 2. The last played aged 30-plus to appear for the club was Thiago Silva, who was 39 at the time.

“We are delighted to have him. To have a goalkeeper of his stature, his personality, I think he will bring a lot of qualities. I am sure he can have a straight impact. We spoke, he felt ready to play, so here we go.”

“We will see. It was a decision we thought was good for the team, for the club. Sometimes you have to take tough decisions because this one is an important one. But now we need to look forward.”

On Enzo Fernandez being left out of the matchday squad:

“We assess what is best for the team and considering everything, the situation, we need a team that is focused, with everyone involved that is fully committed and engaged with the game.”

Emiliano Martínez turns 34 on September 2 and by most tangible metrics, the goalkeeper is past his peak.

But it is the intangibles that set Martínez apart and why his availability at a knock-down price from Aston Villa convinced Chelsea to seize a market opportunity.

At £7.5m, Martínez could prove to be Chelsea’s smartest piece of business of the summer and there is little doubt he will be box-office at Stamford Bridge.

“I am delighted to be at this football club,” Martinez said. “Coming to Chelsea, for me and my family, was an easy decision to make and I am just over the moon; I cannot wait to get started.

“I want to be successful here. I am someone who wants to win at everything I do and I want to bring that here to this football club because it is a football club that wins titles, so I think it is a good match. I am all passion and I play with my heart. I will give 100 per cent every game, every training session to make the club, my teammates and the supporters proud.”

Xabi Alonso takes charge of his first home Premier League game in charge of Chelsea as they host Brighton at Stamford Bridge. Both sides were in action in two different competitions on Thursday night. Chelsea reached the League Cup third round as they beat Luton 2-0 at Stamford Bridge, with former Brighton man Danny Welbeck scoring on his debut. Brighton meanwhile confirmed their place in the Conference League group stages with a 4-0 aggregate win over Tromso.

Chelsea began their Premier League campaign last Monday in a west London derby against Fulham at Craven Cottage, winning 3-2 in Alonso’s first game as Chelsea boss. Enzo Fernandez was not involved in Chelsea’s squad against Luton on Thursday and has been heavily linked with a move to Manchester City. Alonso was asked about Enzo’s absence on Thursday and did not confirm whether the Argentine would be involved today.

“It was just because of the game today [on Thursday] and we have other players who need minutes,” Alonso said. “[On Wednesday], in the afternoon. It is a decision that I took. Enzo is a good professional. He is training well and I have nothing to say about this. It was just decisions that we have to take thinking about the game that we were playing tonight [Thursday]. We will see for Sunday [today].”

Brighton began their Premier League campaign in emphatic style as they thrashed Aston Villa 4-0 at home seven days ago. Jack Hinshelwood scored twice in that game but will now miss a number of weeks with an ankle injury. They are also without Yankuba Minteh, who has been linked with a move to Liverpool this summer but is unavailable due to injury.

“When the window is closed I demand from him [Minteh] that he is fully committed to this club,” Brighton boss Fabian Hurzeler said. “There are dreams and wishes for players, but in the end we always need to figure out what is best for the club.

“We have had an exchange with him. At the moment he is definitely a Brighton player. It is very important to understand his thoughts but also our planning. As a club we try to develop players. The last few years have shown that the whole environment gave him a lot of trust and belief that he is capable of having this progress. It is always a give and take and he has gotten a lot from us.”

Brighton won both Premier League meetings last season, winning 3-1 in this fixture last September. Brighton have won five of their last eight top-flight meetings with Chelsea. Team news from Stamford Bridge to follow shortly.

#2004. Mirabelli reminisces on Calhanoglu signing and Milan disappointment: “A bitter taste”

Today, Massimiliano Mirabelli has looked back on his time at AC Milan and his favourite signing from his short time with the club.

After arriving before the 2017 summer transfer window, there was hope that Mirabelli would oversee a new era with Milan. However, he never got given the extended period to oversee that change that he’d hoped for.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

Indeed, just a year later, the Elliott fund arrived and he was removed from his role as the Rossoneri truly entered a new era.

Responsible for the signings of Andre Silva, Andrea Conti and most notably Leonardo Bonucci, you wonder what would’ve happened if he’d stayed with the Rossoneri for longer. Nevertheless, with what and who eventually arrived, there’s no point considering the alternative, especially given he took a four-year break after his time with the club.

Speaking to Tuttosport, via MilanNews, Mirabelli spoke about the disappointment of his time with the Rossoneri and his pride in bringing Hakan Calhanoglu to Italy.

“Unfortunately, the experience in Milan was short-lived due to the change of ownership. It left a bitter taste in our mouths because we weren’t given the opportunity to complete a long-term project.

“Roma wasn’t built in a day… The deal that still makes me proud today? The Calhanoglu deal . Without a doubt, the best and most successful gamble of my career. We’re talking about the man who, for me, remains the most complete midfielder in Europe to this day. He has incredible, uncommon qualities.

“I started following him when I worked at Inter. We couldn’t sign him from Leverkusen due to an ongoing lawsuit over his double registration as a minor, which resulted in his suspension.

“That’s why I call it a “gamble”: I wanted him at Milan at all costs, even though he hadn’t played for a year and had essentially disappeared from the radar. I was heavily criticized. But, I repeat, I was convinced I had a boy with enormous potential on my hands.

“The biggest discussion, then, was about his position. We spent hours with Montella and—later—with Gattuso to understand where he could best express himself. At Leverkusen, he’d played everywhere: as a midfielder, as an attacking midfielder, and even as a winger.

“Initially, we played him on the left flank, with an inverted foot, to allow him to cut inside and shoot. But it was clear to me that he had all the makings of a great playmaker. When I suggested it to the right people, they called me crazy…

“Leaving for zero? Don’t make me think about it… It’s unspeakable, unbelievable.”

#2003. Police conduct 'knife sweep' around Crawley Town stadium

Operation Sceptre is a national police campaign aimed at reducing knife crime and serious violence.

Police confirmed the ‘knife sweep’ took place in a Facebook post on Wednesday (November 18).

Did you know with an ad-lite subscription to SussexWorld, you get 70% fewer ads while viewing the news that matters to you.

A force spokesperson said: “As part of ongoing activity during Op Sceptre week, officers have been conducting a knife sweep around the Broadfield Stadium area, no weapons were found during the search.

“Knife crime has devastating consequences for individuals, families and communities.

“These proactive searches play an important role in removing weapons from public spaces, reducing opportunities for violence and helping to keep our neighbourhoods safe.

“Everyone has a role to play in preventing knife crime.

“By working together, reporting concerns and supporting young people to make positive choices, we can help ensure our community remains a safe place for everyone.

“If you have information about knife crime, please report it to Sussex Police online or by calling 101.

“In an emergency, always call 999. or you can report anonymously to Crimestoppers @ https://orlo.uk/Hgay2.”
